clue.text: Comply with order unknown

parts.note: the OBE is the Order of the British Empire, a British honour
Y is one of the algebraic unknowns, alongside X and Z

explanation.surface: Someone is told to fall in line with an instruction whose source is a mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: To comply is to do as you are told, the plain synonym for heeding a command.

clue.text: Notes detached and cast out by censor

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of cast are rearranged

parts.note: Cato the Elder, a Roman statesman, held the office of censor and is known as Cato the Censor

explanation.surface: Musical notes are cut loose and thrown away by an official who vets content.
explanation.walkthrough: Cato the Elder was famous as the Roman censor, hence the nickname that supplies the second half.
explanation.definitionFit: Staccato is the musical term for notes played short and separated from each other.

clue.text: Bladder and hearts lost in city street

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, so losing hearts strips the two central letters of city

explanation.surface: A medical complaint and lost hearts somewhere in an urban road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearts lost' removes IT, the middle of CITY, leaving CY.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyst is a fluid-filled sac in the body, and bladder is a general word for such a sac.

clue.text: Last resort on reaching which former airline improves

parts.note: BEA was British European Airways, merged into British Airways in 1974
mends means repairs or makes better

explanation.surface: A defunct airline gets better once it reaches the very end of its options.
explanation.walkthrough: To be on one's beam ends, a nautical idiom, is to be at the end of one's resources.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes being almost out of money or options, the state of having only a final recourse left.

clue.text: A scene suited for necromancy?

indicators.note: suited suggests the letters have been fitted or arranged anew into a better order

explanation.surface: A setting that would suit someone summoning the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A seance is a gathering to contact spirits of the dead, which is what necromancy attempts.

clue.text: Classic writing makes it personal

indicators.note: makes is read as forms into something new, so the letters of it personal are reformed

explanation.surface: A classic text is said to turn something into a private matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' rearranges IT PERSONAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin prose is writing in the classical language, the exercise of translating into it being a school staple.

clue.text: Setting maybe at Watford Gap?

parts.note: Watford Gap is a well-known service area on the M1, Britain's main north-south motorway; written MI it is a place (French lieu) on the M1

explanation.surface: A question about where a scene might be set at a famous motorway stop.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as MI LIEU, a place on the M1, the British motorway Watford Gap sits beside.
explanation.definitionFit: A milieu is someone's surroundings or social environment, the setting in which they live.

clue.text: Cosy with raised arms

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: arms means weapons such as guns

explanation.surface: Comfortable, despite having weapons held up.
explanation.definitionFit: Snug and cosy are synonyms for warm and comfortable.

clue.text: Get increase extremely tidily, which is crackers

parts.note: read as get in crease: in cricket a batter takes guard in the crease, so to get in there is to bat

indicators.note: extremely asks for the extreme letters, the first and last, of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone tidies obsessively for more and more, which is mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'increase' splits into 'in crease', the cricket batter's marked area; 'extremely' gives TY, the ends of 'tidily'.
explanation.definitionFit: Batty and crackers are both informal words for mad or eccentric.

clue.text: Taking up last book slightly adapted without opening

indicators.note: adapted signals a change of order; slightly because only two letters move
without opening means losing the first letter

parts.note: Revelation is the final book of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone takes up the final volume, lightly revised and missing its start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without opening' drops R from REVELATION to leave EVELATION, which 'slightly adapted' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevation is the act of raising something, and taking up can mean lifting or raising.

clue.text: Chants may be composed by sailor …

indicators.note: composed means put together or arranged, so the letters are assembled afresh

explanation.surface: A seafarer might write songs to sing at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be composed' rearranges CHANTS MAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A yachtsman is a person who sails yachts, a kind of sailor.

clue.text: … it's sweet to hear one give voice

indicators.note: to hear says the letters are what the words sound like spoken

parts.note: one is I, and to give voice is to sing, giving I SING

explanation.surface: Continuing the sailor's songs: a pleasant thing to listen to as someone sings.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links it to the sailor clue before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing is the sugary coating on cakes, so it is something sweet.

clue.text: Union as holding one in celebrity

indicators.note: in tells us the group goes inside the word for celebrity

parts.note: a lion is a celebrated person, as in a literary lion

indicators.note: holding means the word as wraps around the next piece

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A marriage that seems to keep a single famous person in its grip.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a connection or relationship, especially a romantic one, so a kind of joining.

clue.text: Endless uprising of one head over heels?

annotationWithheld.why: Endless uprising of one head over heels? (5): REVOLT less T reversed gives the answer, but the only reversal signal is 'uprising' (also the fodder REVOLT) or 'head over heels' (also the definition), so one word does two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Endless uprising of one head over heels?

clue.text: Those who delight in filth, namely TV characters

parts.note: sc. abbreviates Latin scilicet, meaning namely
The Avengers was a 1960s British TV spy series, its heroes the Avengers

explanation.surface: People who love dirt are said to be those on the small screen.
explanation.walkthrough: THE AVENGERS was a British 1960s spy series starring Steed and Mrs Peel.
explanation.definitionFit: Scavengers feed on refuse and carrion, so in a jokey way they relish rubbish and dirt.

clue.text: Interpret former mass

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a pound is a unit of mass

explanation.surface: Explain an old church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mass' looks like a church service, but it is a weight.
explanation.definitionFit: To expound is to set out and explain, so to interpret is a fair synonym.

clue.text: It's sweet to find many in benefit

indicators.note: in places the next piece inside the word for benefit

parts.note: the dole is British slang for unemployment benefit
C is the Roman numeral 100, a standard crossword signal for many

explanation.surface: It is nice to find a lot of people living on welfare.
explanation.walkthrough: THE DOLE is everyday British for unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolce is the musical direction meaning sweetly or sweet, from the Italian word.

clue.text: Instrument involving some abuse?

indicators.note: some means only part of the word for abuse, so its tail is removed

parts.note: violation means abuse or infringement

explanation.surface: Is there a musical device that features some mistreatment?
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' keeps only VIOLA, the first part of VIOLATION.
explanation.definitionFit: The viola is a stringed instrument, a little larger than the violin.

clue.text: The French step over drain

indicators.note: over says the word is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: pas is the French word for step, as in a ballet pas de deux

explanation.surface: A French dance step performed over a gutter.
explanation.definitionFit: To sap is to drain or weaken, as in sapping someone's strength.

clue.text: Shame about oral outburst going to extremes

indicators.note: about means the word for shame goes around the next piece

parts.note: shame in the sense of what a pity, so pity

indicators.note: an outburst bursts the word apart, so its letters are scattered

explanation.surface: Someone regrets an extreme verbal tirade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shame' means 'what a pity', not disgrace; the definition reads polarity as being pushed to opposite poles.
explanation.definitionFit: Polarity is the state of having two opposite poles, things pushed out to opposite ends.

clue.text: Waste from a plate?

parts.note: off can mean from, as in take it off the table
an L-plate shows a learner driver in Britain, so the plate is L

explanation.surface: Is this leftover food from a dinner plate?
explanation.walkthrough: An L-plate is the red L on a white square fixed to British learner drivers' cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal originally meant the waste parts of a slaughtered animal, the bits that fall off.

clue.text: Disagreement about a dash of reality in romance

indicators.note: about tells us the word for romance surrounds the next letter

parts.note: a romance is a work of fiction

indicators.note: a dash is a small amount, so only the first letter of reality

explanation.surface: A row breaks out over how much truth belongs in a love story.
explanation.definitionFit: Friction means conflict or ill feeling between people, a kind of disagreement.

clue.text: Give new spirit to priest in sheer confusion

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation inside the jumbled word
confusion means the letters of sheer are mixed up

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a title for a priest

explanation.surface: A clergyman in total muddle needs reviving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' suggests drink, but to give new spirit is simply to revive.
explanation.definitionFit: To refresh is to revive or reinvigorate, restoring someone's energy.

clue.text: Run across single copy lacking substance

indicators.note: across means the word for run stretches over the next pieces

parts.note: to fly is to run or flee
single is one, the Roman numeral I
MS is short for manuscript, a written copy

explanation.surface: Someone dashes over with one duplicate of a flimsy document.
explanation.definitionFit: Flimsy means weak or insubstantial, so without any solidity.

clue.text: Audience are captured by this lady

indicators.note: captured by means the word are is held inside the word for this lady

parts.note: her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: Listeners have fallen under a woman's spell.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearer is someone who listens, so a one-person audience.

clue.text: Organise swimmer to reverse aquatic movement

indicators.note: to reverse tells us the two pieces together are read backwards

parts.note: to edit is to organise material for publication
an eel is a swimming fish

explanation.surface: Arrange for a fish to turn back with the water's motion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reverse' turns EDITEEL around as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A lee tide is a tidal current running in the same direction as the wind, so a sea motion.

clue.text: Sometimes boys win, girls lose — or it can go the other way

definitions.text: it can go the other way

indicators.note: sometimes says the answer is there in part of the words, at times running between them

explanation.surface: In a contest boys win and girls lose on occasion, though fortunes may reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'boyS WIN Girls'; 'lose' and 'or' just join the phrases.
explanation.definitionFit: A swing moves back and forth, and an electoral swing can move votes either way.

clue.text: Swindle over burgers?

indicators.note: over says the word is turned over, read upwards in this down light

parts.note: Big Macs are McDonald's burgers, known as Macs

explanation.surface: A con involving fast-food burgers?
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a dishonest scheme, a fraud or swindle.

clue.text: Worry a hit might spoil Dreamliner's quality?

indicators.note: spoil means ruin the arrangement, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Fears that a blow could ruin the Boeing jet's fitness to fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might spoil' rearranges WORRY A HIT; the Dreamliner is Boeing's 787 airliner, grounded in 2013 over battery fires.
explanation.definitionFit: Airworthiness is the fitness of an aircraft to fly safely, a property any airliner needs.

clue.text: Seaside not the first to get drier

indicators.note: not the first means removing the first letter

parts.note: the coast is the seaside

explanation.surface: A beach that is not first on the list for drying out.
explanation.walkthrough: An OAST is a kiln for drying hops, typical of Kent in England.
explanation.definitionFit: An oast is a kiln for drying hops, so a type of dryer.

clue.text: Creature that's doubtful, nevertheless one can be seen

parts.note: yet can mean nevertheless, as in 'and yet'
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A creature whose existence is in doubt is still something you might see.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeti, or abominable snowman, is a beast whose very existence is disputed.

clue.text: Away traversing the globe, able to take it all in

definitions.text: able to take it all in

indicators.note: traversing means the word for away crosses over the next piece, holding it inside

parts.note: absent means away
an orb is a globe

explanation.surface: A traveller going around the world, receptive to everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Away' is the adjective, not a direction: someone away is not present.
explanation.definitionFit: Absorbent describes something that soaks liquid up completely.

clue.text: Toast drunk once in judge's garb

indicators.note: drunk means unsteady and jumbled, so the letters of toast are rearranged

explanation.surface: A toast is raised to the old legal robes.
explanation.walkthrough: The stoat's white winter coat is ermine, which trims judges' robes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ermine is the winter fur of the stoat, used to trim judges' ceremonial robes.
